items.sum: Review of the walkers' 1948 season, including Harry Churcher's National 10 miles win, world 5 miles record and Olympic 10,000 metres, the Nijmegen Shield win and Jack Stirling Wakeley's 24 hours walk.
items.s: WITH THE WALKERS. Review of the walkers' 1948 season, including Harry Churcher's National 10 miles win, world 5 miles record and Olympic 10,000 metres, the Nijmegen Shield win and Jack Stirling Wakeley's 24 hours walk. In our last issue comment was made on our chances of a win in the Junior Championship this year and everyone was very hopeful of adding another one to our many successes in this race. However we have yet another year to wait. The race this year was held at Bradford and at about 7½ miles, after it looked as though we were in a fairly comfortable position, Bert East failed to please the judges and was ruled out. Bert Webb and George Bentley, who had walked together almost throughout, maintained their positions at 4th and 5th and after Bill True and Don Heath had been told of the loss of East, they both got down to it and succeeded in carrying our team into 2nd position. Next year we hope to have the services of Joe Scamell in addition to some new members when our chances should be even better than this year. The Surrey County 10 miles Championship provided us with an easy win, our team being led home by Harry Churcher. In addition to gaining the first two places in the Individual Championship and taking Team honours, our “B” Team were placed 3rd. Our Middlesex Walkers did not meet with quite so much success. After Jack Rutland had received one of his few disqualifications, our Cadogan team managed to finish 3rd, Enfield beating us into the place by 1 point. A fortnight later thousands of Londoners witnessed the first athletic event ever to be held in Hyde Park and saw Harry Churcher cut out a terrific pace which took him further in front at every step. The race was, of course, the National 10 miles Championship and Harry's time of 75.10.4 must be the fastest ever accomplished on the road. Needless to say, he retained his title as also did the Club in the Team event. We, therefore, become the initial holders of two new trophies—The London Shield given by the Evening News, and the Ingram St. Dunstans Cup given by Mr. Ingram of St. Dunstans. Bert Ea[illegible]t of the “B” Team walked well to finish 8th and get a place in the Surrey Team which tied with Middlesex for 1st place and contained three of our men, viz., Harry Churcher, Charlie Churcher and Bert East. Of 23 teams to finish, our “B” Team was placed 6th, only 10 points behind the third team. The following week Charlie Churcher took a small team down to Chichester for the trek from there to Portsmouth. The race resulted in Charlie setting up a new course record. Bert Clayton walked well to finish 4th and with Alan Robins and Joe Wilson making the second half of the team, we finished 2nd to Enfield. In the postponed Woodford Green Open the following week we were without Harry and Charlie Churcher, and although our lads were well placed, with Bob Readman (3rd) leading them home, we could only get second to the promoting club who naturally were out in full strength. The Regents Park 15 proved the biggest catastrophe of the season. Apart from Charlie Churcher, who although beaten into 2nd position by Charlie Megnin and returned almost same time as last year, everything went wrong. Our “A” Team men were disqualified almost in a procession. First Bert East, then Colin Sutton and then Joe Coleman. Despite this we managed to finish 4th one place in front of the “B” Team who gave a good account of themselves. The following week we were invited to take a team down to Halton for a match with the R.A.F. Although the majority of our opponents were Air Force Apprentices they showed great keenness and it looks at if Fred Herring is going to produce some real talent in a couple of years' time. After the race we were entertained to a first class meal and a good time was had by all. And so to the National 20 at Sudbury. Our teams were supported by what must be the biggest crowd of Club Members and friends ever seen at a road race. Our Road Captain, Charlie Churcher, surprised most people by not adopting his usual get-a-way method and the opening stages of the race were unusually slow. Later on, however, Charlie developed stomach trouble and was obliged to fall back. About the same time Colin Sutton had trouble with his shoes and lost a lot of ground. In the centre of the field, however, our Vice Captain, Jack Bidgood, was doing some excellent work holding together about half a dozen of our walkers which no doubt had much to do with the ultimate result of the race. On recovering from his trouble, Colin Sutton battled bravely on recovering position after position and eventually caught up on Jack Bidgood and Co. Charlie, however, had continued to drop back and with our friends, Surrey W.C., holding two places in the first five, a win for us seemed out of the question. Eventually our lads finished in a procession with five consecutive placings from 18 to 22 and backed up by George Bentley, Joe Wilson and Joe Coleman, we succeeded in taking the Nijmegen Shield with our eight walkers in the first 48, an excellent performance on which all are to be congratulated. In the meantime the Track Season had opened with a 2 mile walk handicap on 1st May. Naturally the entry was not very big and the race was won by our Track Captain, in the fast time of 14.19 with Syd King 2nd and Joe Scamell 3rd. Three weeks later the second Track Handicap attracted a much larger entry and resulted in a win for Don Heath with Bill True 2nd and young Jimmie Coates 3rd. On the same evening a not too successful Novices' race was held, the only two competitors being introduced by the aforementioned Jimmie Coates. The following Saturday we sent a team to Leicester for the “Round the City” Walk and against strong opposition came out winners, a good omen for the 50 kilometres. And so we come to the most notable success in the Club's history for many years—our Track Captain's achievement in setting up a new World's record for 5 miles. Unfortunately this was held on the same day as the Club Championships and Harry was therefore deprived of the Club support which he deserved. Our thanks are due to Surrey W.C. who so ably assisted in the management of the race in the absence of our own members who were unable to be present. Following this splendid effort, Harry then went to Tooting and successfully defended his two miles title, holding off Bob McMullen and Joe Coleman who finished 2nd and 3rd respectively. The following Monday we staged our increasingly popular Inter Club Contest at Tooting. An entry of nine teams was one more than last year and all the four races were well supported. The total of 55 walkers was an increase of 14 over the previous year. In the absence of Harry Churcher and Bob McMullen, our chances of success were much reduced, but we eventually came out winners with 106 points to Highgate Harriers 102 with Surrey W.C. 3rd. In the Southern Counties 2 miles Championship at Uxbridge, four of our walkers competed and once again Harry led the field to win in the excellent time of 13.53, eleven seconds in front of Jim Morris and beating Bert Cooper's 1935 time of 13.54. Mac and Joe both succeeded in gaining Southern Standards. And so we come to the last R.W.A. National Championship, the 50 Kilometres, which was held at Birmingham. After our win at Leicester, we had great hopes of gaining our 2nd National Success of the season, but what seemed on paper a good team, failed to materialise. At the half distance, both Bert Clayton and Colin Sutton were forced to retire and although Pat Sapcote and Joe Wilson walked exceedingly well, they were not good enough to get the team a place. However, they both retain their “Junior” status and with Pat Sapcote rapidly improving, he should be a big asset to the teams next year. Jack Bidgood walking as well as ever, led the team home in 12th position with Charlie Churcher two places behind and both qualified for standard medals. Surprise of the race was the excellent performance of Lloyd Johnson who finished 2nd to Rex Whitlock and gave the Olympic Selectors something to think about. On the same day, our fast track men competed in the Kinnaird meeting Team Race, and with the team being led by Harry Churcher scored a convincing win over Highgate Harriers with our Surrey friends third. Our annual Mob Match with Surrey Walking Club at Tooting Bec attracted the very large entry of 35 and scoring 10 aside we emerged the winners. George Atkinson won the sealed handicap with veteran Charlie Speechley 2nd and Alan Robins 3rd. At the White City on 3rd and 10th July respectively, Harry Churcher secured a double win in the 2 and 7 miles walks and with these following on his previous successes, we had great hopes for him at Wembley in the 10,000 metres. However, perhaps a very heavy summer programme had some effect on Harry, because when the big day came, he was obviously not on his best form, and although he won his heat comfortably, in the final on the Saturday, he was fifth to J. Michaelsson of Sweden. The first five however beat the previous Olympic Record. On 13th/14th August the Surbiton Town Sports Club, with the assistance of Ernie Neville, promoted a 24 hours track walk. Our only competitor, Jack Stirling Wakeley, was known to have been doing some very hard training, and after maintaining an almost even pace throughout the 24 hours, won by the huge margin of 10 miles, having covered the distance of 122 miles 1,411 yards. A month later we came to the Annual London to Brighton Trek and our entry of 12 competitors was the biggest since 1938. Unfortunately Jack Baker was unable to get to the start, but even so we still had hopes of a place. After doing about 35 miles, however, Jack Bidgood was forced to retire with blistered feet and with the remaining men making a brave effort, we had again to be content with 4th place, Team honours going to Surrey W.C. Jack Wakeley, first man home for the club in 12th place, thus becomes this year's holder of the “Belgrave” Cup. Perhaps the most surprising performance of all was that of George Oliver, who, competing in his first Brighton, finished 18th, just outside first class standard and very deservedly won a special handicap prize presented by Charlie Poulter. Thus we come to the end of another Club Year. Successes we have had as well as misfortunes and disappointments. One thing is certain, many of our walkers are reaching the veteran stage and will soon need replacing by younger members if we are to maintain our position as one of the leading clubs. In the current season, every effort should be made to increase the number of Junior walkers as it is hoped to have a sufficient number to put on the race for the new Junior (under 21) Cup presented to the Club by Tommy Green and also to form the basis of some strong teams for the future. items.label: No. 104
items.sum: A run of short club notes: news of members at home, abroad and in the Services, appointments, a death, novices' races, social evenings and coaching.
items.s: A run of short club notes: news of members at home, abroad and in the Services, appointments, a death, novices' races, social evenings and coaching. Sunday morning strolls have recommenced and start from Wimbledon Station at 9.30 under the guidance of Charles Churcher. Both runners and walkers are welcome. * * * * Battersea Park Track has been re-opened for training but sports meetings will not be allowed for some time yet. * * * * A Get Fit Class will be conducted by our Chief Coach, George Clay, at Belgrave Hall each Tuesday evening, commencing January 4th, at 7.15. Sprinters are particularly invited to attend. * * * * Charlie Smart who although now “almost” settled in Germany is, however, still busy training and racing. He sends his greetings and hopes to be back for some of the big championships, time and circumstance permitting. * * * * George Clay passed the A.A.A. Grade 2 Coaching test, first time. Hearty congratulations, George. He has also passed the County Judges Official test. * * * * Max Quackenbos, now settled in New Jersey, sends greetings and regrets he was unable to get over for the Games. * * * * Wally Rispin, who helped us in many team races in pre-war days, is back with Blackpool & Fylde where he was the leading runner during the last winter season. * * * * We are indebted to Fred Brunning for a new urn at Belgrave Hall. * * * * Wilf Anderson, who is off to Germany on a tour of duty and may not be back for some months, sends greetings to his many friends. * * * * Dan Patience, who is now happily married, has settled in Scotland and the proud possessor of a bonny son—whom we have now welcomed as a Belgravian. * * * * Congratulations to “Ian Michael” on his selection of fathers. I understand his Mother is doing well, but what about poor old Joe? Ian has already been nominated as a member by his grandfather, Tommy Askew. Tommy, I understand, has just celebrated his Golden Wedding Anniversary. Congrats, Tommy. * * * * Sergt. Bernard Eglinton writes that the R.A.F. have moved him to Ismalia where there is a track on which he is trying to perform. He sends greetings to all. * * * * Jack Shields and Johnny Briggs went up to Oxford University for the Michaelmas Term and we wish them well academically and athletically. * * * * Geoff. Osmint, now a gunner in B.A.O.R., sends greetings and says he couldn't attend the A.G.M. for this reason. * * * * A cheery letter arrived recently from Life Member Ernie Musselbrook, a former cross country captain, with all good wishes to the Club. * * * * Our good wishes go to Len Cheesley and Julian de Ruyter who have recently been swallowed up by the Services. * * * * Incidentally it is not generally known that by a Committee ruling there is no obligation on members called to the Services under the National Service Act to pay subscriptions, if they have notified their translation from civilian life. Of course if finances are good the Hon. Treasurer would like to hear from you but it's up to you! * * * * Willie Nankeville has resigned and says he intends devoting his time to building up the local newly formed club, Old Woking A.C. * * * * Martin Williamson, our Junior Cross Country champion, is already busy on the track and recently won the Mile for St. Catherines College at the Cambridge University Freshmen's Meeting, and represented Cambridge University v. Oxford in the Inter-Varsity Relays on November 20th. * * * * Len Camin is busy as Hon. Secretary of the Eltham United F.C., but still hopes to show his paces on the track. * * * * On December 11th there are 3 miles novices races for walkers and runners, so interest your unattached friends right away and bring them along to try themselves out. * * * * At long last the Belgrave Winter “Secret” has been disclosed to members. But one date has yet to be revealed—the date of the Ricketts Shield Race—sorry cads! * * * * Les Cohen has recently been appointed Assistant Hon. Secretary of the Southern Counties C.C. Association; Jack Chapple has been appointed to a similar office in the South of Thames Association C.C. and Ernie Duffett has been elected a Vice President to the same Association. * * * * We all deeply regret the passing of George Hogsflesh, for so many years Assistant Secretary of the Amateur Athletic Association. He probably had more friends in athletics than any other man. * * * * Social evenings, preceded by a sit-down tea, will be held at Belgrave Hall on the following Saturdays: December 11th; January 29th; and February 19th. items.sum: The new President, W. G. Webb, thanks members for electing him, calls for co-operation and team spirit, and thanks them for the clock presented on his resignation as Treasurer.
items.s: From the President The new President, W. G. Webb, thanks members for electing him, calls for co-operation and team spirit, and thanks them for the clock presented on his resignation as Treasurer. FROM THE PRESIDENT I take this opportunity of expressing my appreciation and thanks for the honour you have conferred on me by electing me President of the Club. There is no honour of which I could be more proud. I am deeply aware of the responsibility of this office and will do my best to carry on in the tradition of my predecessors. In this endeavour I shall be guided by the light they have left burning and sustained by the confidence that I shall have the co-operation of all members. Nothing is more important to the Club than this spirit of co-operation. Our continued success both in administration and in the field of sport must, in the end, depend on the strength of each member's personal sense of responsibility for the affairs of the Club. We must never allow ourselves to leave everything to a small group of enthusiastic members who can be relied upon not only to attend committees but also to shoulder the enormous amount of work entailed by their decisions. " Teamwork " has always been our watchword—more difficult, perhaps, in a big team than a small one, but even more essential. I feel sure that the grand old Belgrave team spirit will carry us forward to even greater success. On a more personal note, my wife and I wish to express our thanks for the very handsome clock presented to me on my resignation from the Treasurership. I shall value it always, not only for itself, but as a reminder of the many happy years I have spent with the Club. W. G. WEBB. W. G. Webb W. G. WEBB President; formerly Treasurer W. G. WEBB

items.label: No. 105
items.sum: The Hon. Secretary's notes on the season: two Senior National team titles lost in eight days, cross-country championship wins, the London-Brighton Relay hat-trick, a new Junior One Mile Championship with Ernie Musselbrook's cup, the summer fixtures, farewell to Colin Sutton, good wishes to members and sympathy to Teddy Gordon on the loss of his wife.
items.s: The Hon. Secretary—Alf. Harley writes: The Hon. Secretary's notes on the season: two Senior National team titles lost in eight days, cross-country championship wins, the London-Brighton Relay hat-trick, a new Junior One Mile Championship with Ernie Musselbrook's cup, the summer fixtures, farewell to Colin Sutton, good wishes to members and sympathy to Teddy Gordon on the loss of his wife. THE HON. SECRETARY—ALF. HARLEY WRITES: We managed in recent weeks a unique performance in Athletics—that of losing two Senior National team titles in eight days! However, we can console ourselves with the thought that no other athletic club was ever in the position of holding two such titles at the same time. There is profit to be found in defeat and virtue in challenging for a title as well as defending it. They'll come back, giving us redoubled satisfaction; and our younger generation of runners and walkers the thrills and zest in attaining the highest things which wearers of Belgrave colours are entitled to expect. * * * We can still win, of course! Our runners provided winning teams in both Surrey and Middlesex Cross-country Championships. The South of Thames Championship was won, despite barring clauses, for the third time in four years, with Derrick Burfitt leading the field home. The Southern Championship, too, was held, although it must be admitted not so convincingly as on some former occasions; and our walkers have always been prominent in all their racing, and once again retained the Surrey County titles with ease. The London-Brighton Relay gave us a really first class win despite determined opposition from 24 other clubs. We accomplished our second hat-trick of wins in this series of races, and have won this event more times than any other club in the history of nineteen races over the familiar course. This year's race was undoubtedly the most exciting ever, with several clubs taking the lead at various points and more teams than ever before with a possibility of winning, with only ten miles to go. However, Belgrave prevailed as so often before; with Birchfield, Tipton and Reading striving to the end—gallant and sporting opponents as ever. * * * To our already long list of Club Championships has been added yet another—a Junior (under 19) One Mile Championship which will be contested at our Championships Meeting on Saturday, August 6th, for the first time. Happily, a Life Member, Vice President, and former Cross-country Captain, Ernie Musselbrook, has come forward and generously presented a handsome challenge cup for this new championship. He has expressed the hope that this trophy will eventually carry the names of many who will go forward to the Senior ranks and assist the Club to team honours—for Ernie was ever a team man. We gratefully acknowledge his generosity. * * * The only Club Championship without a trophy is the Hop, Step and Jump, and no doubt this will be remedied in due course. It is whispered that a Junior 440 yards Championship may be the next to be considered by the Committee. * * * From the Summer fixture list it will be seen that a very representative range of fixtures has been tabled. We are very grateful to the London Olympiads A.C., for permission to include several events in their programme on June 22nd. It is to be hoped that all members will make the fullest use of the facilities provided and events arranged during the Track Season now upon us. Given the right approach, we can be as effective a force in Track and Field athletics as past years have shown us to be in the realms of Cross-country and Walking. Our Chief Coach and all his assistants, together with the Hon. Secretaries and Captains are anxious to develop and weld our undoubted talent into effective teams; and we have our thoughts and our eyes on the various Relay Championships and on performing creditably in all our Inter-Club fixtures. With the co-operation of every member—determined to do his best for the Club—we can look forward with confidence to the Summer Season. * * * Our good wishes go with Colin Sutton and his wife and Junior Member Robert, on their emigration to Adelaide in far away Australia. We are sorry, indeed, to lose such a fine sporting family and wish them every success in their new environment. Colin has won many Club Championships and assisted the Club to many team wins; and his walking has ranged from 2 to 100 miles. In 1938, he was a member of our winning "Junior", 20 miles; and 50 kilometres R.W.A. Championship teams—a 100 per cent. team member in a 100 per cent. R.W.A. Championship effort, and a unique performance in the world of walking. We shall certainly miss Colin, not only for his abilities but also for his grand sportsmanship and pleasing personality and his great loyalty to the Club. When serving with the R.A.F. in India, he still found time to walk, and finished second in the All-India 50 kilometres Championship—and he still had time to look out for talent for the Club. It is to Colin that we owe the introduction of another grand sportsman and performer—Vern Blowfield—"discovered" by Colin at Service athletic meetings in India and "ear-marked" for Belgrave when still thousands of miles away! All the best to you, Colin and your family; and let's hear from you. Good wishes to Basil Walden, on B.O.A.C. duties in Tripoli; John Briggs and Jack Shields, now studying at Oxford University; to Reg. Ruddick, now qualified for our teams and eager to show his undoubted ability on our behalf; to our Chief Coach, George Clay, recently returned from hospital after an operation; to Harry Thaxter, "Mine Host" at The Sun Inn, Diss, Norfolk, who recently sent greetings to all friends; to E. Thomas Gilbert, who is now serving in H.M.S. Zest; to Don. Arnold, now a corporal in the R.E.M.E.; to our Hon. Secretary, on being elected to the Southern Committee A.A.A., on our nomination, eighteenth of 48 nominations made; to Charlie Smart on getting a Civil Service appointment in this country and so giving us the benefit of his running rather than his Control Commission colleagues and German spectators; to Michael Porter, formerly of Sale Harriers, but now first claim to us on recent Road Race successes. Undoubtedly he will help our teams. We are grateful to Len Marchant who has undertaken the duties of Hon. Press Secretary and does his utmost to ensure that our notes appear in at least ten local newspapers every week. * * * Our profound sympathy goes to Past President Teddy Gordon on the loss of his wife—so well remembered by so many of us. We shall miss Mrs. Gordon at our meetings and functions; and recall with gratitude her many services to the Club in the past. Particularly, one remembers breakfast served on the roadside in the small hours on our Annual All-night Strolls to Brighton; and those many helpful gestures in the early days of the Building Fund. items.sum: Short club notes on members' news: Les. Stokell, Derrick Burfitt, Syd Ring, Fred White, Michael Broadbent, Alan Sexton, Stan Eales, Frank Abberton and David Main, and the Club Stand at the A.A.A. Championships.

items.s: Short club notes on members' news: Les. Stokell, Derrick Burfitt, Syd Ring, Fred White, Michael Broadbent, Alan Sexton, Stan Eales, Frank Abberton and David Main, and the Club Stand at the A.A.A. Championships. Les. Stokell, has now taken a scholastic appointment at a school in Watford and also hopes to have a full season over the country next year. * * Derrick Burfitt, won the R.A.F. C.C. Championship and was third in the Inter-Services race, hopes to be demobbed very shortly. * * * Syd Ring, is out training again and hopes to run in the open long distance road races this season. * * * Fred White, is another who has started training again, and hopes to be running in the Marathon this year. * * * Michael Broadbent, has been playing rugby and finds this very good training and hopes to regain some of his old form on the track this season. * * * Alan Sexton, our Junior A.A.A. 220 yards champion, has been playing for Rosslyn Park First XV, and is being highly spoken of in the "rugger" world. * * * Stan Eales, recently married, was a spectator at the Club 10 miles Championship at Wimbledon. * * * Frank Abberton, also recently married, is now living at Streatham Hill and married life seems to agree with him! * * * David Main, a member of our 1946 winning "National" team, is now running for the East Antrim Harriers in Ireland, and hopes to be over here during the Summer. * * * There will be the usual "Club" Stand at the A.A.A. Championships on Saturday, July 16th, at the White City, seats numbered and reserved at 3s. 6d. each. Members wishing to avail themselves of this privilege should advise Frank Webb, 50, Longford Avenue, Southall, including CASH with order. The "Supporters Club," after a most successful winter season, has now closed down until the autumn, when new members will be welcomed by Les Cohen from whom full particulars may be obtained. * * * Jack Shotter, who has recently returned from India, is now in regular training at Belgrave Hall. * * * Congratulations to Tom Cotton and his wife upon the latest addition to their family. These notes may be a little behind times but I'm sure Patricia will not mind. * * * All Ernie Duffett's many friends will be pleased to know that his wife who has been in hospital for a major operation, is now back home and is very much better. * * * Frank Abberton, Bill Lucas and Len Marchant, having been selected by Surrey County for the Inter Counties Championship at Manchester, finished 41st, 44th and 80th respectively. * * * Our best wishes to Tom Fifield who has migrated to South Africa. * * * Bernard Eglinton, our Derby member, a sergeant in the R.A.F., writes from Ismailia (Egypt) that he is missing Wimbledon Common and the comradeship of Belgrave Hall. He sends his best wishes to ALL. * * * Arthur Allen, now in the Artillery, sends greetings from Plymouth where he is keeping fit as a P.T. Instructor. * * * Tony Whincup has followed his wife to Crewe where they are now settling down. He has joined a local club but is not too happy about it. Thanks a lot Tony for the telegram of best wishes for the "National." * * * Our thanks are due to Edward Greenwood for his assistance in taking out a youth's pack at Belgrave Hall each Saturday afternoon. This is a little known service performed. * * * We must also thank Micky Pyer for all his work amongst the "youths," the results of which will be forthcoming in the future. * * * Frank Elson is, we regret to report, again very ill and waiting to go into hospital for another operation. All his many friends will wish him a speedy recovery. * * * Our thanks to George Atkinson and Syd Roberts for getting the B.N.L. into circulation again. * * * Bob Readman won the Met. Police 10 miles Walking Championship at Imber Court on February 24th, and a month later was second in the National Police Championship. * * * Harry Churcher won the London Business Houses 7 miles Walking Championship on January 8th, at Southgate, and R. D. McMullen was second. * * * Jack Rutland was third in the British Workers 10 miles Walking Championship at Enfield on February 19th, in 83m. 5s.; McMullen was fourth and J. H. Robins fifth. Martin Williamson was selected to run for Cambridge University in the Mile Relay against Oxford, in the Universities Relay Meeting and he also represented Cambridge University in the Annual Oxford and Cambridge Track Meet at the White City in March. At Cambridge on December 4th he very ably led home Cambridge "B" team to an overwhelming victory over Oxford "B." * * * They do things slightly differently on the Continent than we do here in England. Our war-time member, Etienne Gailly (Steve) and Belgium Olympic Marathon hero has been awarded the annual Grand Prix d'honneur for the outstanding athlete of the year 1948; and at Brussels he was awarded the annual "Trophie National du Merite Sportif," chosen on account of his Olympic Marathon performance. He was also placed fourth in a poll recently organised by Belgium's leading sports daily to find the most popular athlete for the year. * * * Albert Frost was fifth in the Civil Service 5 miles Championship at Addington. * * * Recent R.W.A. appointments include Harold King, Alf Harley and Charles Warren as Judges, Syd Roberts as Supplementary Judge and Dick Savage as Timekeeper. * * * Bert Ellsey has also been re-appointed delegate from the Southern Counties Cross Country Association to the Southern Committee A.A.A. and also been re-elected a Vice President of the Surrey County A.A.A. * * * Other recent appointments to the Surrey County A.A.A. are Harry Parker and Jack Chapple as Vice Presidents and Joe Coleman, Dick Savage and Charlie Jones elected to the Committee. * * * Congratulations to our old friends the "Poly" on their third place in the "Southern," ably helped by our own Poly member, Jimmy Wood, who was 23rd. Ron Hughes, who was with us during the war, was an excellent fifth and Rene Howell was 160th. * * * Congratulations also to Sutton Harriers on their splendid win in the "National." In a field of nearly 450 runners they scored 128 points, 121 in front of the second team, Reading. * * * Geoff. Pearson was sixth in the Inter-Banks Championship over 4½ miles at Hayes (Kent), and third in the Westminster Bank 5 miles Championship. * * * Bill Lucas was second in the Insurance Championship over 5 miles at Coulsdon. Incidentally, he has been asked to hold himself in readiness for the British Empire Games in New Zealand in 1950. * * * Amongst his other achievements during this winter season, Eddie Short was fourth in the London University Championship, over 4¾ miles at Roehampton. Fourth in the Universities Athletic Union 7 miles Championship and second in the Inter University match against Cambridge University. He represented the English Universities against Scottish Universities, when he finished dead heat first with three other team mates. * * * Len Marchant won the London Business Houses Championship over 5 miles at Wimbledon. * * * Bert Clayton won the Hants County 10 mile walk Championship on January 29th at Eastleigh, in 85m. 45s.; with Percy Wright 4th in 90m. 49s. Forces, and asks for changes of address. HON. TREASURER'S NOTES The following donations to general club funds have been received during the past six months from the following members, and I wish to express the thanks of the committee for their generosity:—Messrs. G. A. Atkinson, O. Horwood, £2 2s.; J. G. Coleman, T. H. Cotton, T. C. Jones, £1; F. S. Bradnum, 11s.; L. J. Cohen, A. A. Harley, H. E. Footer, A. E. Taylor, F. R. Webb, 10s.; E. Musselbrook, 5s. These are additional to donations given by various members to the Open Walk Prize Fund, and the Children's Party Fund. * * * Many members seem unaware that Club Subscriptions become due in September of each year, and cover the period up to the following September. A member who joins at any time after September pays a full year's subscription, but his next subscription becomes due the following September. It will assist me considerably if subscriptions are paid promptly, without waiting for a reminder. * * * It may not be generally known that the Committee have ruled that members serving in H.M. Forces under the National Service Act may be excused payment of their subscriptions, but it is essential that such members should advise the Hon. Treasurer that they wish to take advantage of this concession. If no communication is received we have no means of knowing the member is entitled to be excused payment. * * * One other small but important matter, do please keep the Hon. Secretary or Hon. Treasurer informed of all changes of address, and so save the bother of having communications returned "Not known." G. A. Atkinson G. A. Atkinson donation £2 2s. O. Horwood O. Horwood donation £2 2s. Of this number nearly 300 have paid their subscriptions for the current year, whilst of the remainder, 215 have paid for last year, leaving nearly 150 who have not paid anything since the Club year 1946-7 or earlier. items.s: The "Overseas" Trophy—Percy Wright says: Percy Wright reports that the "Overseas" Trophy fund raised from wartime "Airgraphs" stands at £6 19s. 6d. and appeals to members who served overseas to subscribe so a cup can be bought. THE "OVERSEAS" TROPHY—PERCY WRIGHT SAYS: Remember it? We planned it for after the war with the money that we made on those "Airgraphs" you chaps sent me. Unfortunately, the man that bought the "Airgraphs" died and this source of income died with him. We had, however, succeeded in getting quite a tidy sum—£6 19s. 6d., to be exact. I had hoped to plan something else to raise the money to a sufficient sum to purchase a suitable trophy, but my present distance from the Club quarters is not convenient. It has been suggested to me that I make an appeal to all those who served overseas and would like to see the idea of the "Overseas" Cup materialise to send along a subscription. Well, lads! what about it? Send your cheque, postal order or stamp, either to me or to the Hon. Treasurer, not forgetting to mention what it is for. We should also be pleased to have any suggestions on how the trophy shall be awarded. This appeal is addressed to all Club members who served overseas and not only the Walkers. 34, Elgar Road, Sholing, Southampton. Percy Wright PERCY WRIGHT PERCY WRIGHT Sholing Southampton

items.sum: Syd Roberts reviews the walkers' winter season: the club 5 miles Handicap, the Highgate, Enfield, Belgrave, Cambridge Harriers and Met. Police Opens, and the Horwood Cup Race.
items.s: Walking Notes Syd Roberts reviews the walkers' winter season: the club 5 miles Handicap, the Highgate, Enfield, Belgrave, Cambridge Harriers and Met. Police Opens, and the Horwood Cup Race. WALKING NOTES By SYD ROBERTS The winter season opened with our usual 5 miles Handicap, with a match against the Police in conjunction. In all, 40 Walkers started, including 25 of our members, a promising start for the new season. In the absence of Harry Churcher, Bob McMullen led the field, followed by Bob Readman and Smith of the Police. F. Tasker, rapidly improving, won the Handicap, with Brian Shepherd second and Don Heath third. In the first Open of the Season, Highgate Harriers 7, at Parliament Hill Fields, we entered three teams, but neither Harry Churcher or Joe Coleman were amongst the competitors and with Jack Rutland nowhere near his last year's form, we had to be content with third scratch team. A fortnight later came the Enfield Open and although it was the same day as the Club Dinner, this did not deter the majority of our Walkers from making the long journey to Enfield for the race and back to Clapham for the dinner. This race was the beginning of a winning sequence, practically all our men walking up to form. Harry Churcher soon set up a good lead and remained unchallenged. In addition, we took scratch team honours with the "B" and "A" teams second and third respectively in the Handicap and George Oliver second in the Individual Handicap. Next came our own Open with, as usual, the biggest entry of the season. Although a little below last year's total of 248, there was an almost total absence of provincial entries due, no doubt, to the ever increasing cost of travelling. The weather, however, was not very kind to us and as a result of a very dense fog a number of competitors were unable to reach Wimbledon. Despite the conditions, 182 Walkers faced the starter, and once again Harry Churcher led throughout. Backed up by McMullen, Readman and East, we succeeded in retaining the "Berman" Trophy. Our "B" team once again finished second in the Team Handicap and Len Fletcher, proving he can still show some of them the way round, finished fourteenth and was awarded the prize for the first unplaced member. Our thanks are again due to those loyal members who contributed to the prize fund and also to the large number of officials who gave such valuable assistance under very trying conditions. A fortnight later we held the Horwood Cup Race. A field of 22 juniors lined up for the start and once again Bert East led them home, with George Bentley second and Pat Sapcote third. Charlie Speechley, still having a go, won the Handicap, with George Atkinson second and Joe Scammell third. On the same day a Novices 3 miles race resulted in a win for E. Evans, one of our new Walkers. The following week our Walkers travelled to Bexley Heath for the Cambridge Harriers Open and continued our winning sequence in the scratch race with Harry Churcher leading the team home. Once again the "B" team were second in the Team Handicap. With the new year, came the Met. Police Open at Imber Court. In a field of over 200 starters, Harry Churcher soon took the lead on this very fast course and the scratch team added yet one more to their list of Open wins, this time Charlie Churcher getting his first place in the winning team. With the continued run of Handicap placings our teams were unable to get in the first three. The following Saturday, we held our 10 miles Club Championship, which, needless to say, was once again won by the invincible Harry, with Bob McMullen second and evergreen Bob Readman third. Alan Robins, the first "junior" to finish, showed a marked improvement and was placed fifth. A match in conjunction resulted in the Police being beaten by 55 points. And so we come to the Junior Championship at Enfield on February 5th. Although we had a reasonably good team it was generally thought that competition would be keen between Cambridge Harriers, Highgate Harriers and ourselves, and not much was known of the strength of Midland and Northern Clubs. Sheffield, however, proved to be very strong and their scoring four finished in the first dozen. Coleman of Highgate and Long of Cambridge, having been ruled out of their respective teams by the referee, we were given second place with 48 points. Unfortunately for us this was later reversed by the A.A.A. Southern Committee, the revised placings being Highgate second, 52 points, Cambridge third, 53 points, Belgrave fourth, 56 points. Alan Robins again walked exceptionally well to lead the team home with Bert East, George Bentley and Pat Sapcote supporting him. George Oliver, who had been off form recently, was relegated to the "B" Team, but was fifth club man to finish. In the Surrey Championship we once again secured double honours, Harry Churcher leading the team in his usual style, followed by Charlie, Mac and Bert East. Charlie was again selected as Team Captain for the County, the other three also being members of the team with Syd James as reserve, for the Inter Counties Championship at Leicester. Our Cadogan members in the Middlesex Championship did not fare so well, with the exception of Bob Readman who finished second to Jim Morris, the team being fourth. Bob was selected to represent Middlesex and Alan Robins, finishing fourth in the Kent Championship the same day was selected to represent that county. And so to Leicester for the National 10. Keen competition was once again expected from Highgate and Cambridge, with little known of Sheffield apart from their "Junior" win. Harry Churcher and Allen of Sheffield set the pace from the start, but unfortunately at about 3½ miles Harry failed to please one of the Northern judges and was disqualified. This left Sheffield in a very strong position and at 6½ miles they had three men in the first seven with a total score of 31 points. Our first four were well placed at 6, 8, 9 and 19, 11 points behind Sheffield, with Charlie Churcher rapidly moving up. Jack Rutland, however, was having some trouble and slowed up slightly. Highgate occupying fourth, fifth, sixteenth and twenty-fourth positions were a few points behind us. Towards the last mile, Mac showed signs of tiring and whilst Charlie moved up still further, eventually overtaking Bob Readman, Mac slipped back to tenth position. Jack Rutland clung on desperately, maintaining his position to the finish, but with one or two in the first twenty dropping back, Highgate improved their third and fourth positions gaining seven points against our loss of one. Sheffield also lost a few points over the last stages, but this did not prevent them maintaining a clear lead, and with L. Allen nearly two minutes in front of Jim Morris, they took double honours, with Highgate in second place, beating us by one point. items.label: No. 105
items.h: A Review of the Cross Country Season
items.sum: Ernie Duffett reviews Belgrave's 1948-49 cross-country season: wins in the Surrey, Middlesex (as Cadogan A.C.), South of Thames and Southern championships, but a poor showing in the National at Birmingham.
items.s: A Review of the Cross Country Season Ernie Duffett reviews Belgrave's 1948-49 cross-country season: wins in the Surrey, Middlesex (as Cadogan A.C.), South of Thames and Southern championships, but a poor showing in the National at Birmingham. Although naturally hoping to do as well as last season, when we cleared the board so far as the major championships went I think that apart from our dismal showing in the "National" race, that our ruuners can be said to have done well throughout the season. We started by failing to secure a place in the South of Thames "Junior," but this was due more to the selection of our teams than to the failure of our runners. Eric Herbert, who was our second man home in 15th position, had been put in the "B" team and we had to go back to 57th for our fourth scoring "A" team runner. Even so we only lost third place by 1 point, but with Eric Herbert in our "A" team we should have been an easy second to Surrey A.C., who won the race with the low score of 30 points. We won both the Surrey County and Middlesex County events, the latter by reason of our members who ran for their second-claim club, Cadogan A.C. Frank Abberton was the individual winner of the Surrey race and Derrick Burfitt only failed by a couple of yards to repeat this performance in the Middlesex event. In the South of Thames 7 miles Championship at Horsham, we repeated our win of last season and have now won this race three times in the last four years. As the winning six scorers are barred from competing again, it will be seen the considerable strength which we have, and it is this that makes us all the more optimistic about the future. In addition to again winning the "Dewar" Shield we also won the "Colman" Cup awarded to the club which has the lowest score for its complete team of 12 runners, and indeed our score for 12 men was lower than some clubs had for their team of six counters. The Southern race was held at Camberley and with a field of over 350 runners, team scoring was naturally high. Even so, our winning total of 183 points was the highest ever in the history of this event, so I think the best that can be said was that we were the best of a poor lot! Here again we won the "Oddling-Smee" Cup for finishing our complete team before any other Surrey club, and we actually had 11 men in the first 96 scoring places, which in such a large field is excellent running. So to the "National" at Birmingham and although we were not too optimistic we certainly expected at least to get a place, and so continue our unbroken list of placings in this event since our initial third place in 1933. There was a huge field of 449 runners and it does seem as if some qualifying rule should apply to clubs entering this event as some of the competitors were hopelessly outclassed and a large number were lapped. We had some consolation in winning the "Charles Otway" Cup, awarded to the first club, outside the placed teams, to finish its team of 9 men, but hope that next year we shall once again be up to the front and fighting it out with the Sutton lads, who will be hard to displace from their positions as champions. items.s: South of Thames "Junior" Team Race Report of the South of Thames Junior cross-country team race at Farningham, where Belgrave's "A" team was fourth, one point off third, with the placings of the A, B and C teams. Held at Farningham on November 6th over a rather tough 5 miles course and with an entry of 50 teams, a record for the race, a field of 316 runners faced the starter. We were drawn on the outside but after the initial breakaway Archie Bedford was seen to be lying second and Eddie Short was also well up. At the half-distance the latter was in fourth place but there was no sign of Archie, and it later transpired that he had dropped out owing to shoe trouble at about 2 miles, which was certainly very bad luck for his team-mates. Eric Herbert was our second man but running for "B" team. This was won easily by Surrey A.C., who had a strong four and they all ran well. The Portsmouth R.N. boys surprised many by gaining second place and Aylesford Paper Mills just pipped our "A" team by 1 point for third place. Eddie Short was rather unlucky in just missing a place, he finished 4th in last year's race, and Mike Heard and Arthur Bruce both did well in such a large field. Eric Herbert and George Durrant both upset the team selectors by their forward running, but these things have happened before and no doubt will occur again. items.sum: Report of the 50th South of Thames cross-country championship at Horsham, won by Derrick Burfitt from Peter Curry, with Belgrave first team and winners of the Colman Cup.
items.s: South of Thames Championship Report of the 50th South of Thames cross-country championship at Horsham, won by Derrick Burfitt from Peter Curry, with Belgrave first team and winners of the Colman Cup. The 50th annual cross-country championship was held at Horsham on February 12th, over a 7½ miles course. A field of 187 runners turned out and the course arrangements and loud speakers for the benefit of the spectators were very good, and quite up to "National" standard. Over the first small lap Peter Curry, the Olympic Games steeplechase representative was in the lead closely followed by Derrick Burfitt. On completion of the first big lap, Curry and Burfitt had drawn away from the rest of the field and were running stride for stride. When they came in sight of the finish, however, Derrick was well in front and he won in fine style in the good time of 44 mins. 13 secs. with Curry clocking 44.44 in second place. Our lads had gradually been working their way through the field with Len Marchant always up with the leading bunch, and eventually Mike Heard was 11th with Jack Brown 13th and George Durrant 14th, which was a very good show on their part. J. McDonald was our sixth man in 28th position and Len Adams 38th and Lou Bush 40th gave good support. With such forward running we easily won the "Colman" Cup for the first club to finish their complete team of 12 men, and Ken England is to be complimented on finishing the course after having a bad time. items.s: Southern Counties C.C. Championships Report of the Southern Counties cross-country championships at Sandhurst, where Belgrave retained the senior team title and the Oddling-Smee Cup, with Youths, Junior and Senior placings. These were held at the Royal Military Academy, Sandhurst, on February 26th, and the dressing arrangements were first class. A field of over 350 runners turned out for the Senior 10 miles race, and after a very fast start across the playing fields, the field then had to do 4 laps out in the country which consisted of running through woods with some steep inclines included. Ted Stimpson was always well up with the first dozen runners, but Vern Blowfield was suffering with shoe trouble and was gradually dropping back while Len Herbert and Marchant were striving to hold their places, but things did not look too good for our prospects of retaining our title as Southern champions. However, on the final lap, Blowfield started to pick up again and Steve Charlton and Tom Carter were also coming through the field to consolidate our scoring positions. Even so, with our six men in 46 we were not too optimistic and were frankly surprised when told that we had won the team race once again. We also retained the "Oddling-Smee" Cup awarded to the first Surrey club to finish their 12 men, and so brought the trophies back home again for the second successive year. In the Youths race Michael Stearman ran well to finish 22nd, but the rest of our boys lacked racing experience. The Junior race saw Eddie Short having his usual bad luck in finishing 4th, he must be getting used to this position now, and Arthur Bruce was 47th, but here again they lacked support. items.s: English Cross Country Championships Report of the English (National) cross-country championships at Bromford Bridge, Birmingham, where Belgrave lost their title to Sutton Harriers and finished sixth, with the club's Youths, Junior and Senior placings. On March 12th we journeyed to Birmingham for the "National," held on the Bromford Bridge Racecourse, although the runners actually ran outside the course, which included a cinder path, a mud splash and a descent something like a shute used at a swimming bath. As the seniors had to do 4 laps of this gruelling course the spectators were given a good view of the racing, but what the runners thought is another matter. On the first small lap of the senior race Vern Blowfield was up to the front with Aaron, the eventual winner, but could not hold his position and gradually fell back. Our other men were well placed to begin with but as each lap came round, with the exception of Steve Charlton, they seemed to go further and further back while our most dangerous rivals, Sutton Harriers, had their men well up and going forward all the time. We soon realised that we had lost our title of "National" champions, but must say that the Sutton lads deserved their win and are indeed worthy champions. Vern Blowfield was our first man home, 18th, and Steve Charlton did well in being 58th, and after him our next four men packed well but were, of course, too far back to stand a chance of getting placed in the team race. However, we need not be too discouraged, as we have some good youngsters coming along to take the older men's places, and surely our chaps cannot run so bad next year, or at least, we hope not. In the Junior race Eddie Short again ran well and although having a couple of falls down the "shute," he was our first man home in 13th place. C. W. Walker, the winner of our recent road race for Novices, did well in his first "open" race to finish in 34th position, but we missed the services of Arthur Bruce, who could not get leave from his unit. The Youths race saw a large field and Mike Stearman was our first runner in 48th place, and once again the rest showed a lack of experience in running in such a large field. items.s: Surrey (Senior) Cross Country Championship Len Marchant's report of the Surrey senior cross-country championship at Earlwood, won by Frank Abberton with Belgrave first team, followed by the County Junior race and Ernie Duffett's note on the County Youths' race at Addington. As was the case with most of the counties on New Year's Day, Surrey held their championship under very trying climatic conditions. The 7½ miles course at Earlwood was completely waterlogged owing to the very heavy rain, this coupled with a strong, bitterly cold wind caused the majority to "swear" once again that "it's a mug's game!" Those who were fortunate enough to get in front of the field over the first mile stayed there, and during the whole race the leading men remained the same, Frank Abberton, Bowering (S.L.H.) and Barry (H.H.H.) fighting for first place, Bill Lucas and Marchant being a few places further back. In the final check-up it was found that George Durrant had run exceptionally well to finish 15th. Frank Abberton ran exceptionally well to win such a gruelling race after having to battle all the way. Len Herbert did not find the going to his liking and finished no nearer than 19th closely followed by our Poly member, Jimmy Wood, who had ran steadily throughout to finish 23rd. This is our 14th win in this championship. 1, F. Abberton, 44.1; 7, W. Lucas, 45.13; 8, Marchant, 45.21; 15, Durrant, 46.15; 19, L. items.h: Middlesex County Championship, Trent Park, January 1st
items.sum: Harry Shields reports on the Middlesex county cross-country championship at Trent Park, won as a team by Cadogan A.C. (a team of Belgravians), with Derrick Burfitt second by one second to Olney.
items.s: Middlesex County Championship, Trent Park, January 1st Harry Shields reports on the Middlesex county cross-country championship at Trent Park, won as a team by Cadogan A.C. (a team of Belgravians), with Derrick Burfitt second by one second to Olney. Cadogan A.C. were represented by a full team of Belgravians and the race was held in a howling gale over a three lap course totalling 7½ miles. The venue is that over which it is proposed to hold the 1950 "National" and is a good sporting course of undulating grassland. Our team got away to a good start and quickly showed to advantage with Derrick Burfitt and Vern Blowfield among the leaders. Derrick and Olney (T.V.H.) soon sorted themselves out and together fighting all the way Olney eventually won on the tape by taking the "proverbial deep breath," the timekeepers giving Olney one second's advantage. The team won with a score of 85 pts., the second team being another 45 pts. behind. Bush winning the handicap. Our 7 Miles Cross Country Championship was held on December 11th, and a record field of 55 runners faced the starter, of whom 48 finished. At the half-distance Ted Stimpson was in the lead followed by Len Herbert and George Lucas, but when the runners came in sight of the finish Len Herbert was in front and running strongly. The other positions were unchanged except that Mike Heard was hot on the heels of George Lucas, followed by Arthur Bruce and Martin Williamson, and it is pleasing to see these youngsters giving the senior members such a strong challenge. Jimmy Wood and Rene Howell (our Poly members) were also in the field and Bert Footer surprised a few by his forward running. L. Bush deservedly won the handicap while George Durrant continued his improved form to gain second place with Eric Bishop beating his brother, Alan, for third prize. items.s: "Macher" Shield Race Report and full result of the club's 10 miles cross-country championship for the Macher Shield on January 29th, won by Vic Blowfield, with J. McDonald winning the handicap and a note of the 1928 placings. The 10 Miles Cross Country Championship for the "Macher" Shield was held on January 29th. It was a glorious afternoon and a field of 45 faced the starter, Albert Macher, the eldest son of the donor. At the half-distance Vic Blowfield and Frank Abberton were together in the lead with Bill Lucas and Len Marchant fairly handy, but the rest of the field were already well strung out. When they came in sight of the finish Blowfield was in front with Frank Abberton still second, but Len Marchant had come through to third place. There was rather a gap after the first three home but the rest of the field then arrived at regular intervals with Tom Carter and Stan Davies having a desperate sprint to the finishing line, which Tom won by inches. When the handicap had been worked out it was found that J. McDonald was the winner and he certainly ran well in his usual determined style and there was a dead heat for second place between Jack Brown and "Ginger" Charlton, which the latter won on the toss of a coin with Brown taking third prize. There was a good crowd present and we were pleased to see our old club champion, Arthur Clark, who won this race twice, and as a matter of interest the 1928 placings were: 1, A. Clark; 2, E. A. Duffett; 3, A. D. Pyer; 4, W. G. Webb; 5, H. E. Footer; and we are pleased to see that four of the above are still very much with the club after 21 years have gone by. * Denotes dead heat. items.sum: Report and full result of the club's five miles road race at Belgrave Hall on March 19th, where the first two went off course and the handicap went to Albert Frost.
items.s: Five Miles Road Race Report and full result of the club's five miles road race at Belgrave Hall on March 19th, where the first two went off course and the handicap went to Albert Frost. FIVE MILES ROAD RACE. Held at Belgrave Hall on March 19th, and a field of 54 runners faced the starter, who was our old club champion and ex-Empire Games 6 miles champion, Arthur (Nutty) Penny. Len Marchant set a fast pace round the first small lap and a bunch of about eight runners were well up with him. When they came in sight again Vernon Blowfield was in the lead with Jack Brown running stride for stride with him, and then, unfortunately, they went slightly off the course, and so came home well in front of the rest of the field. Ted Stimpson, who was third, kept to the correct road and the rest of the field followed him, so it was decided to ignore the first two runners' placings in the handicap result. This resulted in a win for Albert Frost, who had run well above his recent form, and Alf Taylor took second prize by 1 sec. from George Chantler. The first nine home all completed the course, which is reckoned to be over the stipulated distance, in under 30 mins., and these times augured well for our chances of winning the London to Brighton Relay for the third successive year. items.s: Inter-Club Matches Reports of a senior and junior match against Mitcham A.C. at Roehampton and a "B" team match against Old Croydonians A.C. at Belgrave Hall. INTER-CLUB MATCHES. On November 13th we visited the Mitcham A.C. quarters at Roehampton for a senior and a junior match. The senior race was won by Len Marchant, and of the first six home five were " Bels." Mitcham, however, provided the first three in the junior race and beat us by 19 pts. to 49 pts. Leading positions in the senior match were: 1, L. M. Marchant, 31.56; 2, W. E. Lucas, 32.3; 3, R. F. Towndrow, 32.4; 4, D. Brickwood, 31.10; 5, L. W. Herbert, 32.23; 6, E. Stimpson, 32.29. Team scores: Belgrave Harriers 109 pts; Mitcham A.C. 189 pts. * * * On November 20th we had the Old Croydonians A.C. at Belgrave Hall for a "B" team match, but when they only brought along five runners, the first of whom finished 5th, and scoring four aside we won by 10 pts. to 26 pts. items.sum: Report and results of the club's Boxing Day meeting on Tooting Common track: 100 yards, 3 miles walk, 2 miles run and weight put handicaps.
items.s: Boxing Day Meeting Report and results of the club's Boxing Day meeting on Tooting Common track: 100 yards, 3 miles walk, 2 miles run and weight put handicaps. BOXING DAY MEETING. Held at Tooting Common track with a white frost showing everywhere, and as a result the track was bone hard. Entries in the sprint were not too good but six heats with two or more runners in each were made up, and with six runners in the final a good race was seen. G. S. Robinson, one of our promising junior sprinters, was first with another junior in R. B. Thomas second, and John Briggs now demobbed and up at Oxford University gained third place, with Alan Sexton, our Junior A.A.A. 220 yards champion, a close fourth. The Walk was won by Percy Wilson with 5.45 start, and Harry Churcher walked well from the scartch mark to gain second place. A new member in S. James, off 4.45, was third. A good field was seen in the 2 miles run and Eric Bishop, off 260 yds., was a good winner with Martin Williamson, off 180, second, and Lou Bush, off 300 yds., third. Derrick Burfitt ran well, off a back mark, to run through to sixth position, and looks to be in for a good season over the country. 100 Yards (heat winners): R. B. Thomas (7); A. D. Sexton (1); P. V. items.h: Cambridge University at Belgrave Hall on January 22nd
items.sum: Bill Lucas and Alf Taylor report a "B" team match against Cambridge University (with Kent A.C.) over the club 7 miles course, won by Cambridge; the report calls Martin Williamson "our own" while the result marks him (C).
items.s: Cambridge University at Belgrave Hall on January 22nd Bill Lucas and Alf Taylor report a "B" team match against Cambridge University (with Kent A.C.) over the club 7 miles course, won by Cambridge; the report calls Martin Williamson "our own" while the result marks him (C). CAMBRIDGE UNIVERSITY AT BELGRAVE HALL ON JANUARY 22nd. Bill Lucas and Alf Taylor writes:— This match, which was run over the Club 7 miles course in ideal conditions, was designated as a "B" team fixture, but it soon became apparent that more than a "B" team was needed to defeat the Cambridge runners, which included three men who participated in this year's Varsity race, ably backed by their second strings. Len Marchant set a fast pace from the start and quickly gained a 30 yds. lead, which was not lost until the beginning of the second lap when Bill Lucas with Gorton and Palmer, of Cambridge, in close attendance, took up the running. This order was maintained until the Windmill when the two Cambridge boys went away together from Lucas to win by 16 secs. in the good time of 39.33, which incidentally had rarely been beaten in our own club championships over this same course. As Cambridge had their scoring six in the first nine places, including our own Martin Williamson, who was 5th, they finished easy winners with 30 pts. against 57 pts. by Belgrave. It was good to see Minahan racing again after a long lapse through injury and it is hoped that he will be able to continue his training. Good performances were put up by Adams (11th), England (12th) and Chantler (14th) to complete our scoring six. Kent A.C. also joined in this match, their first runner being Gravely in the 8th position. Result:—1, Gorton and Palmer (C), 39.33; 3, W. Lucas (B), 39.49; 4, Marchant (B), 40.4; M. items.s: Thames Valley Harriers Road Relay Report and leg times of the Thames Valley Harriers road relay at Cranford on March 26th, won by Birchfield, with Belgrave "B" third and "A" fourth. THAMES VALLEY HARRIERS ROAD RELAY. Held on March 26th, at Cranford, and we had entered five teams, although our National team men were having a rest from competitive racing. Birchfield had sent down a useful four runners and they held off all challenges to win a good race. Our "A" and "B" teams had been having a battle royal in 2nd and 3rd positions, but Alec Olney on the last "leg," put up a really smashing performance to clock 23.4 for the journey of about 4½ miles, and took his club into second place. Our "B" team finished third with our "A" team fourth, and as there were four sets of prizes, our lads were well satisfied with the result of their efforts. Eddie Short ran the best of our men with Bill Lucas showing next best time and Steve Charlton and Tom Carter, despite a fall over a bicycle during his "leg," also ran well. It was unfortunate that our "D" team failed to close in owing to being a runner short and it is a pity that runners do not advise someone if they find they cannot turn out for a race. items.s: The Track Season for 1949 Ernie Duffett sets out the club's 1949 track fixtures and championships and asks for entries to be sent to him. THE TRACK SEASON FOR 1949. Ernie Duffett writes:— Your Committee have arranged a full list of fixtures for both Senior and Junior members, and there are also a number of "B" team matches for the lesser lights. We open our track season on May 7th with a club meeting at Tooting, and we then have matches arranged for each Saturday in May. The County Championships are on June 4th, with Surrey at Motspur Park and the Middlesex at Southall. On the Whit Monday, Surrey County are holding their Junior 4 x 110 yds. relay and the Senior Mile Medley relay at the "Charlotteville" meeting at Guildford, which is a very good grass track. items.label: No. 105
items.sum: Terry Bateman reviews the club's field events prospects for the coming season event by event and urges members to train and support the coming meetings.
items.s: Field Events Gossip Terry Bateman reviews the club's field events prospects for the coming season event by event and urges members to train and support the coming meetings. FIELD EVENTS GOSSIP. Terry Bateman writes:— This coming season, it is hoped, the Club will improve so that we shall at least attain if not exceed our pre-war standard in Field Events. We have a number of new members to support this hope. "Steve" Gibson, in the High Jump, has already achieved quite good performances with "the Scissors" style. All the winter he has been gradually evolving the "Western Roll" technique and before the end of the season should show improved performances. With Dick Negus back in training, and, we hope, back to his form of two years ago, we should be quite strong in this event. We hope also to have the assistance of John Boxall now that his examinations are nearly at an end. Unfortunately, our chance of having Wilf Anderson, our Club Champion, out are practically nil as he is on a tour of duty in Germany with the R.A.F. "Steve" Gibson, Les Christmas and Stan Botwright will be our main hopes in the Long Jump, but it would be good to see Geoff Wood taking part in this event more often as it is felt he has good possibilities. Geoff Wood and Les Christmas, together with Bert Machell, will be our Hop, Step and Jump men. Geoff Wood should get near A.A.A. Standard, and Les Christmas with more training getting over 40 feet. In the heavy events we do not seem to have any new blood. Jock Mackenzie in the Discus should again show improvement and will be backed up by Sid Jones and Bill Sutton. Sid and Bill will be our Shot Putters, but Jock Mackenzie and Les Christmas have possibilities if they only get down to training. There is a need for more men in both these events and some of those heavyweights who find running a bit too arduous might think seriously of taking up either or both events. In the Javelin we hope to have the assistance of the two old stalwarts. Charlie Melchior and George Powell. However, it is to Alan Dunn, Geoff Jarvis, Arthur Allen and Terry Bateman we look for improved performances and from at least one, distances approaching, even if not beating those achieved by the old stalwarts in previous years. Geoff Jarvis, who is in the R.A.F., is also quite a good hurdler both over the High and 440 yds. distances. We hope he will be able to get leave for the more important matches. John Briggs, now at Oxford, is also a hurdler of possibilities, but we cannot expect him to be able to turn out until the end of the term. As far as the Juniors are concerned our strength is rather unknown although we have a large number who are interested in Field Events. Doug Whitehead, who was very promising last year in the Javelin and Shot, is now in the Forces and will probably have difficulty in getting along for matches. John Morrison should show improvement in the Shot. Terry Batemen, our new Field Events Hon. Secretary, needs all your support in his first season to make it a really successful one. So you are expected to rally round him not only to improve your own performances but that of the Club in general. Your coaches for the Field Events have felt that some have not made as much use of their services as they would have liked but it is still not too late. Therefore, if you are really keen on improving your performances, contact them and you will find they are willing to give the benefit of their advice. The biggest day for Field Events is the Polytechnic "Sward Trophy" meeting at Chiswick on May 14th. Every event is included and we have to provide two men for each so it is expected you will get down to training immediately. This is followed by the County Championships on June 4th. We should like to see these Championships really well supported. Even if you cannot hope to get a place there is always a standard medal to be aimed at. The Kinnaird Trophy and the Waddilove Trophy now include most Field Events and we must have strong teams to support the runners. The Club Championships are fixed for August 6th at Tooting. All the way through the season there will be inter-club matches in which Field Events will be included as well as handicaps at all events for which we expect your full support. A number of Open Meetings are including Field Events handicaps and our support of these is needed. Not only will it give you added opportunity for competition but only by this means can the country discover new talent. Details of these meetings can be obtained during the season from the Hon. Secretary or Captain. items.sum: The Junior Captain and sprint coach Frank Simmons writes to the juniors about coaching, the A.A.A. Junior Relay, the P.T. class and Sunday rambles for the coming track season.
items.s: Frank Simmons Writes The Junior Captain and sprint coach Frank Simmons writes to the juniors about coaching, the A.A.A. Junior Relay, the P.T. class and Sunday rambles for the coming track season. FRANK SIMMONS WRITES. Dear Juniors, This is a reminder to you all that the summer season is fast approaching, which means quite a lot of you will be thinking of returning to the track. Some of you have already met me, some have yet to meet me, but to all I will be pleased to see you. I may as well tell you now that I am your junior sprint coach and that I work in close co-operation with George Clay, who is our chief coach. For Field Events Juniors, Charlie Jones and Bill Sutton are your coaches. Incidently, you did not make enough use of them last summer, so perhaps you did not do as well as you thought. This can be remedied by you alone, by turning out for coaching regularly. Micky Pyer is middle distance coach and if you pay attention to him you will do well, as I am sure if you have any running in you Micky will help you to put ti to the best use. To the sprinters, George Clay and I have ambitions but can only achieve them if you pull your weight. We have had a crack at the 4 x 110 yds. A.A.A. Junior Relay and only just failed. We want it this year and with your help we will get it. Also I want more to endeavour to enter into County and other individual championships. In short, we want to make our Club feared at shorter distances as the Cross Country boys are and our walkers are over their distances. I must warn you that the preliminary training may be boring but stick it as it all leads to bigger things. Who knows, you may be Belgrave's first Olympic Sprint Champion. I know I am aiming high but it can be done and the coach's job is to help you. Tuesday evening P.T. class under George Clay is going well at Belgrave Hall, but again I would like to see more of you there. It is designed to help you. To all the juniors, all-day Sunday rambles are taking place fortnightly and again I would urge you to come along. Charlie Jones leads and I can assure you of a very good time in good company. Wishing you all a very good track season and assuring you of the help of all your coaches. YOUR JUNIOR CAPTAIN. items.sum: Dave Martin-Shepherd on the season's socials at Belgrave Hall, followed by a report of the Annual Dinner at the Express Hall, Clapham Junction, where Tommy Green presented his trophy to Harry Churcher.
items.s: Social Section Dave Martin-Shepherd on the season's socials at Belgrave Hall, followed by a report of the Annual Dinner at the Express Hall, Clapham Junction, where Tommy Green presented his trophy to Harry Churcher. SOCIAL SECTION Dave Martin-Shepherd writes:— May I say how enjoyable it has been to see the Club members with their wives and friends at the Socials held at Belgrave Hall during this season. The support given by wives and friends to the sport in the afternoon and to the social in the evening make these occasions something to remember. I should like to take this opportunity to thank all who have assisted me, especially those who helped at the Boxing Day Party cabaret and nearly did for me at the same time. I do feel that the social side of the Club is very important and that it all goes to make Belgrave such a formidable power that it is in athletics. If you have not been to a social may I admit that we have always expected both you and your friends so what about it next season? * * * The Annual Dinner which was held at the Express Hall, Clapham Junction on Saturday, November 6th was again a huge success and the hall was filled to capacity. President Bill Webb must have felt particularly proud presiding over such a gathering which included many well known administrators in both walking and running world and not forgetting the many well known "champions." It was very pleasing to have with us our Olympic Champion, Tommy Green, and his wife, and the opportunity was taken to get him to present to Harry Churcher the handsome trophy he has given to the Club for the outstanding Club performance of the year. Tom Cotton "Esquire" was a worthy toastmaster. Our thanks are indeed due to our Social Secretary, "Dave," for the splendid evening he put on for us. The dance following was very ably conducted by Bert Ellsey. items.sum: The new co-editors thank retiring editor Harry Parker, now President of the E.C.C.U., and promise improvements including a suggestion page.
items.s: Editorial The new co-editors thank retiring editor Harry Parker, now President of the E.C.C.U., and promise improvements including a suggestion page. Dear Fellow Belgravians, We humbly present to you the Belgravian issue for November, 1949. In doing so we first of all give thanks to your past Editor, Harry Parker. Many onerous duties have come Harry's way during his career with Belgrave, extending over many years and all he has tackled with great enthusiasm and with remarkable achievements. He is not the kind of person to relinquish his commitments without very good reason, but now he finds his official duties in the service of athletics at least one too many, and he has been obliged with very great regret to hand the editorship over to new co-editors. As we all know Harry has certainly plenty on his plate and always has had and now that he is President of the E.C.C.U., he finds it hard to carry on as Editor. In congratulating him on his great honour, we also thank him for his great work to the club. As for ourselves, your new co-editors, we follow in the wake of Harry Hare, Ben Knifton, Alf Harley, Gordon Doubleday, Freddie Bradnum and Harry Parker. We are fully conscious of the great work and standards built up and maintained by our predecessors and we assure you of our best endeavours to keep up this standard. We have several ideas for the possible improvement of our magazine which we hope you will all approve but, as with this issue we are endeavouring to bring all reports up-to-date, pressure of space prevents us introducing new ideas on this occasion. We do intend, however, to issue another Belgravian at a very early date and to include these ideas, chief among which will be a "Suggestion page," and we ask those of you who have any suggestions, to let us have them in as brief a letter as possible, but let us get this issue among you first and we hope you will find the next one and subsequent issues interesting, entertaining and topical. Best wishes, Your EDITORS. Harry Parker Harry Parker retiring Editor of The Belgravian; President of the E.C.C.U. items.label: No. 106
items.sum: Report of the club's 1949 Annual General Meeting, at which Bill Webb was re-elected President and officers' reports were heard.
items.s: Annual General Meeting—October 8th, 1949 Report of the club's 1949 Annual General Meeting, at which Bill Webb was re-elected President and officers' reports were heard. The attendance at this meeting was not as large as was hoped nor as large as we have the right to expect. However, a very representative gathering of somewhere about 80-90 members assembled to elect your new officials and committee and to define the club policy for the year 1949-50. Once again our popular President, Bill Webb, was elected to the premier office of the club and this was received with unanimous acclamation. Secretary Alf Harley's report struck a very optimistic note in spite of one or two reverses during the past season. In reading his report we had a moment or two of thought for the passing of three of our club members: dear old Charlie Cook, Tom Sullivan and Rowland Rowbottom, which we all regret. The Hon. Treasurer's report showed us that although we were spending much more money than we received in ordinary receipts and subscriptions, we were able to balance our club budget through the efforts of the Supporters' Club. The Building Fund is in an extremely healthy state and a word of appreciation was given to Les Cohen and his supporters. Our Treasurer, Syd King, has done a wonderful job in carrying on after that great treasurer, Bill Webb. We all thank him for his work and congratulate him on his achievements. We were sorry and considerably concerned, however, when he warned us that this would be his last year of office. Under the capable chairmanship of Bill Webb the meeting progressed. Your officers and committee were duly elected and during the ensuing phase under the heading of "Other Business," the future policy of the club was discussed in a most rational and democratic manner. One left the meeting convinced that the management of the club was again in most capable hands and with a feeling of confidence for the season 1949-50.
