items.sum: Stage-by-stage account of Belgrave's win in the Brighton road relay of April 1949, the club's sixth win in the race.
items.s: The "Brighton" Relay held April 2nd, 1949 Stage-by-stage account of Belgrave's win in the Brighton road relay of April 1949, the club's sixth win in the race. RUNNING NOTES Starting from Mitcham, our runner on the first stage to Purley was Derrick Burfitt. He did well to finish 5th in 30 mins. 6 secs. On the next stage to Merstham, Ted Stimpson held his place and his time was 27.25. Then Frank Abberton tackled the up-hill stage through Redhill and ran a fine race to take us up into 2nd place with a time of 23.9. On the next stage, Jack Brown took us in front and running well clocked 28.7. Len Herbert went off on the 5th stage which had been slightly altered. Jimmy Wood, our Poly. member, caught and passed him but Len managed to hang on to second place with a time of 25.29 and handed over to Albert Frost who did well in putting up the fastest time for that leg which is now only just over 2 miles and his time of 10.51 kept us in second place. Vern Blowfield went off on the long stage to Handcross and soon passed his man to put us in the lead once again. His time was 31.25. Len Marchant was our next but he lost the lead to Green of Reading and clocked 21.40 for his stage. Eddie Short went off on the up-hill climb to Patcham. He passed the leader and in clocking 21.34 did the second fastest time and gave us a lead of 11 secs. over our nearest rivals. Bull Lucas, running the last stage, as usual, did not give his opponents any chance of getting on his shoulder and although Green of Birchfield took his team into second place, Bill finished an easy winner and moreover did second fastest time of 17.49 for his leg. The order for finishing was 1, Belgrave, 3 hrs. 57 mins. 35 secs; 2, Birchfield, 3.57.52; 3, Tipton H., 3.58.35. This makes our 6th win in this classic road race, a feat which no other club has performed and moreover, is our second series of three wins in a row as we won in 1934-5-6 and then again in 1947-8-9. items.s: Match v. South London H.—May 7th Track match at Tooting in which South London Harriers narrowly beat Belgrave in both senior and junior contests, with club handicap results. Held at Tooting, this was our opening fixture of the summer season and we had senior and junior events with a few club handicaps on the programme. The senior match was a very close affair and our visitors won by the very narrow margin of 2 points. They also won the junior match by 5 points. Mike Broadbent finished second to Grieve in the 100 yards. John Cope was second to Pugh in the 440 and we had first two home in the 880 in Len Marchant and Jack Brown. Bill Lucas won the mile and Eddie Short won the two miles, beating Ted Stimpson. George Powell's win in the javelin, was our only success in the field events side and we also won the medley relay. In the junior match our only winner on the track was Alan Sexton in the 220 yards, but a new member in H. R. Delger, won the javelin and we also won the 4 x 110 yards' relay. Final scores were: Senior.—S.L.H., 63 points; Bels., 61 points. Junior.—S.L.H., 25 points; Bels., 20 points. Handicap events:.— 100 yards: 1, A. Law (11); 2, D. Clements (11); 3, P. Morrison (7½). items.h: Match v. Ealing Harriers and Walton A.C.—May 14th
items.sum: Gordon Stewart Trophy match at Drayton Green won by Walton A.C., with Belgrave second and Ealing third.
items.s: Match v. Ealing Harriers and Walton A.C.—May 14th Gordon Stewart Trophy match at Drayton Green won by Walton A.C., with Belgrave second and Ealing third. Once again we visited the Drayton Green Track for the inter club contest for the "Gordon Stewart" Trophy, promoted by the local club. We congratulate Walton on their win, but as they had two Olympic men in their team we were not disgraced. Once again the two short sprints proved our undoing and we had to run Alan Sexton in the 100 yards in order to put up a show. Bill Lucas won the mile with A. Bedford second and Derek Burfitt gave Nankeville a good run in the half mile. In the two miles team race we had the first three home, with Jack Brown, Vern Blowfield and Len Marchant finishing in line. We lost the Medley Relay where John Cope tried hard to hold Nankeville over the first 880 but the Walton man gave his team the lead which they maintained to the end. Final scores were: 1st, Walton A.C., 34 points; 2nd, Belgrave H., 29 points; Ealing H., 11 points. Also on the programme were a few junior events and Walton again proved successful in these by scoring 27 points to our 18 and Ealing's 10. items.h: Match v. Walton A.C. and Thames Valley H.—May 21st
items.sum: Triangular track match at Stompond Lane in which Belgrave and Walton A.C. tied on 56 points with T.V.H. third.
items.s: Match v. Walton A.C. and Thames Valley H.—May 21st Triangular track match at Stompond Lane in which Belgrave and Walton A.C. tied on 56 points with T.V.H. third. On May 21st we visited Stompond Lane for a triangular match. Here again a few junior events were included in the programme, also a 120 yards hurdles event and the home club scored in these events. They also did well in the short sprints with Lewis scoring a double and our only placed man in these events was Les Christmas, third in the 220. R. C. Sharp, running in the 440 yards, gained third place. Len Marchant put up a new ground record in the 880 yards when he beat Alec Olney in 1 min. 58 secs. Olney, however, won the mile with A. Bedford fourth and in the 2 miles Reg. Ruddick beat off the challenge of L. Field of T.V.H. to win in 9 mins. 56 secs. Our Latvian member, A. Bergvalds, was second in the shot and then won the discus throw and should prove a great help to this branch of the club. N. Gibson was second in the high jump and evergreen George Powell was second in the javelin event. We gained third place in the 4 x 110 yards relay and the final scores were: Belgrave and Walton A.C. 56 points each, T.V.H. 49, a very closely contested match and much enjoyed by all, including our supporters who turned up in good numbers. items.s: Junior Match at Croydon Return junior match against Whitgift Middle School on 30 May, won by the school 52 points to 20, several of whose placers were Belgrave members. The return match against the Whitgift Middle School was held on May 30th and a good crowd of our youngsters made the trip. Our only winner of the evening was John Morrison in the 440 yards. Wolton was second in the 880 and Hazel second in the mile. Sexton and Marshall running for their school, again completed a double for the first two places in the 100 and 220 yards and the school also won both the relay races. Cooper and Stinton who were first and second for the school in the high jump are also members of our club and so it can be seen that although we lost the match, our club members were well to the fore. items.s: Surrey County Championships Belgrave members' placings at the Surrey County senior and junior championships, including county records for Alan Sexton, John Grey and Len Herbert. The Senior and Junior Championships, with one or two exceptions were held at Motspur Park on June 4th when the club did quite well and the result of the club's coaching methods was clearly seen. Alan Sexton performed a double in winning the 100 and 220 yards and in the latter event he set up a new county record of 22.7 secs. Another club member set up a new county record when John Grey, in the Junior Discus, recorded a throw of 137 ft. 3 ins. The 3 miles championship was held at Tooting on July 6th and Len Herbert set up a new county record in the fast time of 14 mins. 38.6 secs. Bill Lucas unfortunately had to retire with leg trouble, otherwise we may have had the first two home. We are glad to see Len Herbert getting back to form as he had a disappointing season over the country and we hope that he will keep it up and lead our lads in their effort to regain our lost title of National Champions. items.s: Match v. Mitcham A.C.—June 8th Senior and junior match against Mitcham A.C. at the News of the World Sports ground; the seniors won and the juniors lost by a point. This meeting held at the News of the World Sports ground, comprising both senior and junior matches, resulted in a win for the seniors by 49 points to 34, but the juniors lost their match by 1 point—12 to 11. Mike Broadbent and Gordon Lowers were first two home in the 100 yards, while Jim Beaumont and Heathfield were second and third in the 440. items.sum: Belgravians' performances at the 1949 A.A.A. Championships, including Harry Churcher's 7 miles walk win and Charlie Smart's standard medal.
items.s: A.A.A. Championships at White City—July 16th Belgravians' performances at the 1949 A.A.A. Championships, including Harry Churcher's 7 miles walk win and Charlie Smart's standard medal. On Friday evening Michael Broadbent competed in Heat 1 of the 100 yards and was beaten by Mac Bailey in the fast time of 9.9 secs. He qualified to run in the second round on Saturday afternoon but was 5th in a 10.2 secs. heat! Geoff Jarvis won his heat in the 440 yards hurdles in 56.9 secs, and was third in the final won in 56.7 secs. In the 880 yards John Cope was fifth in his heat. In the mile, Derrick Burfitt won his heat in 4.20, but in the final was seventh in 4 min. 19 secs. Marchant and John Brown also competed. Charlie Smart made a gallant effort in the 6 miles on Friday evning and eventually finished fifth in 30 min. 42 secs., thus gaining a standard medal. Ruddock and Towndrow also ran. Harry Churcher won the 7 miles walk in 52 min.41 secs. on the Saturday morning after a deluge of rain which left the track waterlogged. Len Herbert was sixth in the 3 miles in 14 min. 37 secs. Both Smart and Ruddock had another "bash" but after their gruelling 6 miles on Friday only Smart gained a standard. The 2 miles walk was held at Birmingham on July 29th and Harry Churcher was beaten 10 yards by the Swede, Borgesson. items.h: Match v. Cambridge H. and Dartford H.—July 27th
items.sum: Report of the match at Charlton Park lost narrowly to Cambridge Harriers, with the junior match also lost to Cambridge.
items.s: Match v. Cambridge H. and Dartford H.—July 27th Report of the match at Charlton Park lost narrowly to Cambridge Harriers, with the junior match also lost to Cambridge. This was held at Charlton Park and after a very close tussle with the home club, they won by the narrow margin of 2 points. Basil Walden was second in the 100 yards and Lionel Grimshaw won the 220. Jim Heathfield was third in the 440, John Cope won the 880 in 2 mins. 1.6 secs., while Bill Lucas won the mile in 4 mins. 30.2 secs. Charlie Smart, home on leave from Germany, turned out in the 2 miles and clocked 9 mins. 45 secs. to win a good race with Ted Stimpson second. We won the medley relay, but Cambridge gained first places in all three field events and this finally decided the match in their favour. Final scores were: Cambridge H., 47 points; Belgrave H., 45 points; Dartford H., 7 points. In the junior match we gained second place in the 100 yards, also in the 220 and were third in the 880. Ken Hill was second in the mile. Ian Law second in the discus and E. Gowland second in the javelin. Scores were Cambridge H., 26 points; Belgrave H., 24 points; Dartford H., 15 points. items.sum: Report of Belgrave's final handicap meeting of the season at Tooting Bec on 17 September.
items.s: Final Club Track Meeting—September 17th Report of Belgrave's final handicap meeting of the season at Tooting Bec on 17 September. The final handicap meeting of the season was held at Tooting Bec on Saturday, September 17th, and although the entry for the 3 miles run was up to standard, the other events on the programme were not too well supported. The final of the 100 yards was a good race and Clements just beat Kemp with Mitchell third. The 880 yards saw Ken Cuff beat A. Tapley by about one foot with J. S. Tranter third. The mile race for unattached novices only attracted four entries and P. W. Adams, a younger brother of our own runner, displayed promising form in winning this event. In the 2 miles walk, Harry Churcher walked in fine style and eventually finished second to Joe Scamell, with George Oliver third. In the 300 yards, Alan Sexton was on scratch mark and duly qualified for the final by winning his heat. The final saw the field well away but Alan went after them and on coming into the straight came through strongly to win a great race in 32.3 secs. R. Holtum, a new member was second with Johnny Morrison third. The 3 miles run was the main event on the programme with Jack Brown, the back marker off 60 yards and the limit man on 500. C. Walker who won our novice road race last winter, was off 120 yards and running strongly he eventually took the lead followed by Len Marchant and they finished in that order with Rene Howell, our Poly. member, third off 160 yards. Eddie Short lost a shoe but pluckily kept going and Archie Bedford came through to finish a good fourth. Jack Shields and Ken England were also well up and a new member in J. H. Braggington also did well in his first club race. W. Hadley scored a good handicap double by winning the javelin and long jump events and in the former George Powell was second with A. Machell third. Alan Law was second in the long jump with Frank Simmons third. items.sum: Terry Bateman's review of Belgrave's 1949 field events season, highlighting Geoff Jarvis, John Grey, Bergvalds and Peter Lowe.
items.s: FIELD EVENTS REVIEW Terry Bateman's review of Belgrave's 1949 field events season, highlighting Geoff Jarvis, John Grey, Bergvalds and Peter Lowe. Although the year has brought a slight improvement in the standard of field events it has been due to outstanding individual efforts rather than to improved general performances. However, our juniors show great promise and we must see they are given every encouragement. One of the outstanding and commendable performances of the season was the 440 yards hurdles run by Geoff Jarvis in 56.7 secs. which gave him third place in the A.A.A. Championships. This was followed by another good performance in his winning the R.A.F. Championship and in being chosen as reserve for England v. France match for the same event. Previously Geoff had concentrated on the high hurdles and the change to 440 yards has obviously been most successful. Another outstanding performance was that of John Grey's discus throw of 137 ft. 3 ins. which won him the Surrey County Junior Championship and broke the existing record by about 18 ft. He also gained a standard medal in the A.A.A. Junior Championships. Our weakest events have been the high and long jumps. Conditions were not improved when mid-way through the season we lost the services of Steve Gibson, one of our most promising high jumpers who went into hospital for an operation on an old war wound. We take this opportunity of wishing him a speedy recovery and hope to see him out at the winter training sessions John Sinton a junior who has given good support to our senior matches is to be congratulated on his 5 ft. 6 ins. jump in the Police match at Imber Court. Both the juniors, Bob Cooper and Jim Purdy, have been jumping well and show promise. We were not too successful in either the Svard or Kinnaird meetings. One of the best performances was that of Harry Delger at the Kinnaird meeting when he threw the junior javelin about 154 feet to gain third place. Bergvalds was the outstanding performer in the club championships. He won the discus and shot, and was third in the javelin. His discus throw of 123 ft. 8½ ins. set up a new club record. Peter Lowe established a new club record in the hop, step and jump, with an effort of 41 ft. 5 ins. Charlie Melchoir retained his javelin title with Les Higgins as runner-up. Our old stalwart, George Powell, has been consistently throwing the javelin over 140 ft. in matches and has been a source of inspiration to younger aspirants. It is intended to resume the field events training periods through the winter months at Tooting on alternate Saturday afternoons. items.s: JUNIOR NOTES F. Simmons's letter to the juniors reviewing their county and Southern successes and announcing winter P.T. and Sunday strolls; it gives J. Grey's county record discus as 137 ft. 8 ins., where the field events review on page 14 prints 137 ft. 3 ins. Dear Juniors, The summer season is now finished and it is with pleasure that I say thank you for your support in both matches and in championships. We had a successful season ending in successes in County and Southern County Championships. Our successes in the County Championship were: A. Sexton, 100 yards in 10.5 secs.; Equals County record. 220 yards in 22.7; New County record. D. Marshall, 100 yards, third; 220 yards, second. Picton, 220 yards. County standard. J. Grey, Discus, 1st. New County record; 137 ft. 8 ins. Southern Counties: A. Sexton, 220 yards, 1st, 23 secs. We had three in the final of the 220 yards and John Morrison gained his Southern standard in the 440 yards. In addition we won the Southern Counties 4 x 110 yards relay. Our congratulations to Desmond Mullen on winning the Irish Junior 100 yards and his second in the 220. Some of you did not do as well as you hoped, but keep trying and success will come and when it does it will be all the sweeter. Some of our junior pals will be leaving our section to go forward to the seniors and our best wishes for continued success goes with them. To all new recruits to our section we give a “ Belgrave ” welcome and assure you all of a healthy and happy time. To our cross-country juniors, we wish you every success in the coming months. It is hoped, all juniors who can possibly attend, will come along to our winter P.T. class at Belgrave Hall. Details will be available later, also Charlie Jones and I are arranging all day strolls from November until April every Sunday, which we hope you will all make an effort to come along to. They are very good for you, in fact, the senior successes were built up on their strolling and I see no reason why you cannot do the same. The strolls will be worked out so that the cost will suit everybody's pocket. I thoroughly understand that some of you have home studies, but when you can make it, come along, you can be sure of a welcome and a good time too. In conclusion, on behalf of the juniors, I convey their congratulations to Harry Churcher on his winning the A.A.A. 7 miles' walk again and also on his new world's record. F. SIMMONS. F. Simmons F. items.sum: Review of Belgrave's 1949 race walking season: Met. W.C. 15, Chichester–Portsmouth, club and national championships, Harry Churcher's records and titles, and the London to Brighton walk.
e: Belgrave Harriers Club 20 Miles' Walk Championship
items.s: WALKING NOTES Review of Belgrave's 1949 race walking season: Met. W.C. 15, Chichester–Portsmouth, club and national championships, Harry Churcher's records and titles, and the London to Brighton walk. Looking back over the season which has just finished, we certainly have not disgraced ourselves. Our wins in Open Races in the South have been up to our usual standard and we have been placed in two of the Senior National Championships. That we can do better there is no doubt, especially do we need some more young members and it is hoped that the coming season will see an improvement in this direction. Continuing our activities, following the National 10, three teams were entered for the Met. W.C. 15 miles at Regent's Park, but alas, before any great distance had been covered, Charlie Churcher was ruled out and our chances of success thereby greatly reduced. This race seems to be very unfortunate for us, as like last year, we suffered more than the usual disqualifications. These included Pat Sapcote and Jack Baker. The unusual distance of the race got the team selectors guessing with the result that two of our “ B ” team men finished before the second “ A ” team man. Outstanding was Bob Readman who held the lead throughout the greater part of the race, but on the last lap he tired rather badly and dropped back to third place. With a team score of 64 points we were very surprised to find that we gained third place. In the Chichester to Portsmouth race on Easter Saturday, Charlie Churcher repeated his brilliant performance of last year by winning the individual honour. As we did not send a very strong team, it was not surprising that we were unable to get better than third place, 9 points behind the winners, Woodford Green. The following Saturday we held our own Club 20 Miles' Championship. As usual, being the first 20 of the season, a number of the starters failed to finish the course, but the 14 who completed the distance walked exceptionally well. Veteran Jack Bidgood, after 20 years with the club, succeeded in winning his first Championship after a well-judged race, followed by Pat Sapcote and Charlie Churcher. And so we came to the National 20 and from the performances of our walkers in the Club 20 it seemed that we had a reasonable chance of success. Unfortunately Bert Webb was unable to make the journey to Manchester and we were without any knowledge of the capabilities of the Sheffield boys over the longer distance. The weather, for Manchester, was extremely good, in fact, no rain fell throughout the day. At the start the two Sheffield lads, Allen and Proctor, made a quick getaway and joined by Lloyd Johnson, set up a good pace. Lloyd however, did not last with them for long and soon began to drop back. Most of our lads walked extremely well and were ably assisted by Harry Churcher, Syd Roberts and Percy Wilson, but despite all their efforts, they were unable to do better than second place, with Charlie Churcher taking third individual honour. Competition for the Nijmegen Shield was very keen. Sheffield being successful, with Woodford Green second and ourselves third. In a new promotion this year, the Watford 25, we entered a small team and succeeded in gaining third place in both the scratch and handicap sections. The last National Championship of the season, the 50 Kilos. was held from the Police Sports Club at Chigwell over a very stiff course. The weather, which was very warm, added to the trials of the walkers and of 73 starters, no less than 31 retired without completing the full distance. These included Charlie Churcher, who developed leg trouble, Pat Sapcote, Fred Herring, Jack Wakeley and Don Heath, so that by the end of the race we had just a bare four left, who finished in fourth position, 2 points behind Woodford. For the Eastleigh A.C. 50 Kilos. on July 16th, Pat Sapcote was unable to make the journey at the last minute, thus depriving us of one of our best men. However, Bert Clayton sprung a great surprise by leading all the way through and eventually winning the individual race, and although the rest of the team walked exceedingly well, they had to be content with second place to Surrey W.C. Jack Bidgood also won a style prize, and Bert Clayton was second in the handicap. On August 23rd we were invited to field a team in Surrey W.C.'s 6 miles road race at Tooting Bec Common. Despite the fact that the fixture did not appear on our summer programme, 12 of our walkers turned out and after a very interesting race, Surrey just managed to win by 103 points to 107. So much for the road walks. On the track Harry Churcher, as is now well known, succeeded in lowering his world's record time of last year for the 5 miles. Walking in excellent style, Harry lapped the track time after time in almost identical times, eventually clipping 10.4 secs. off his time at Motspur Park. In addition to this he succeeded in taking the Surrey County 2 miles' title, the Southern Counties 2 miles title, and on a water-logged track at the White City, the 7 miles A.A.A. title. A fortnight later Harry took second place to Borgesson in the A.A.A. 2 miles but revenged his defeat in the London-Gothenburg Match a week later by winning the 7 miles at the White City in 51.2.2, his fastest time for the distance. This race prevented him from defending his Club 2 miles title and in his absence Bob McMullen, walking in very fine style, became this year's club champion. On June 22nd we had our annual mob match with Surrey W.C. on the track at Tooting, beating them by 89 points to 121, with Joe Scamell (jr.), Brian Shepherd and Mac taking the handicap awards in that order. A “ B ” team match against the Veterans A.C. at Tooting Bec on July 9th also resulted in a win for us. Our Annual Inter Club Walks of 1, 2, 3 and 4 miles proved a great success this year, no fewer than 66 walkers competing. The competition proved to be very keen, eventually resulting in a win for Woodford Green with Highgate Harriers second and us third. A number of our walkers have figured well in Open Handicaps and Veterans' Events, successes being scored by Bert East, Syd James, Charlie Speechley and young Joe Scamell. As usual our Police members figured well in the Barking to Southend Walk. Jack Bidgood was once again second with Bob Readman, Pat Sapcote and Bert Webb following him home in that order. The winning team, “ B ” Division, was completely Belgrave. On August 27th we had a 25 miles match with London Vidarians and Surrey Walking Club. This race next year is to be an Open Event and should prove a good training walk for the Brighton. The race resulted in a win for Surrey W.C. with us second. In the London to Brighton Walk on September 10th, eleven of our walkers started off on the stroke of Big Ben at seven o'clock, to be joined later by a number of supporters. In the early stages, Jack Bidgood, Bert Clayton, Jack Baker, Jack Wakeley and George Oliver, walked in a group with Don Heath and Joe Wilson not far away. Gordon Doubleday, F. Herring, Sid Spencer and Bill Urry, followed at an easier pace. Jack Bidgood eventually went away from the others and at the Chequers Horley was in ninth position. A check at Crawley (29¾ miles) showed that our men had held their positions with the exception of Jack Wakeley who had stopped for a massage. By the time Bolney was reached, Jack Bidgood had improved his position to seventh, Clayton was 16th, Baker 21st and Wilson 27th. With the retirement of Bert Martineau from the Surrey team there seemed a chance that our team would be placed and although Jack Bidgood dropped a couple of places to go back to ninth Joe Wilson moved up to 23rd and at the finish our positions were: Jack Bidgood, ninth; Bert Clayton, 16th; Joe Wilson, 21st; Jack Baker, 23rd, making a score of 62 points and just losing us the third position. So Jack Bidgood became our long-distance champion as well as holder of the 20 Miles Championship. He's a champion to be proud of. His judgment of pace and unflagging stamina throughout the race set a fine example. Bert Clayton was a worthy second and showed his grit in overcoming tiredness in the last few miles. Joe Wilson walked his best Brighton to date and came along in fine style in the latter half to finish remarkably fresh. Jack Baker pluckily stuck it out over the last half to complete the team. items.label: No. 106
items.sum: Note urging Belgravians to thank wives and sweethearts by bringing them to the club's social events on 19 November and 10 December.
items.s: THE LIGHTER SIDE—SOCIAL ACTIVITIES Note urging Belgravians to thank wives and sweethearts by bringing them to the club's social events on 19 November and 10 December. The Social Hon. Secretary, Dave Martin Shepherd, has asked for more space for social activities. We shall certainly give him all we can for the social side is just as important as any other part of the club. In promoting these social events we are really showing our appreciation to the wives and sweethearts of Belgravians who without support and encouragement from their dear ones would never achieve the great performances they do. Do you stop to think what you owe to them. Who washes your running clothes each week? Who looks after the diet prescribed either by yourselves or well-meaning advisers? Who sits and listens over and over again to stories of walking, running and field events until they could scream? Who sits alone night after night waiting for committee men to return, having resignedly relinquished many hours of their domestic life to officialdom of Belgrave? Aye, give them a little in return, and we can assure you that nothing pleases them more than to join in our social activities at the club to whom they undeniably give so much. So make a note of the following dates and come along. Saturday, November 19th. Saturday, December 10th. Dave Martin Shepherd Dave Martin Shepherd Social Hon. Secretary

items.label: No. 106
items.sum: Report of the club's Annual Dinner and Dance at the Express Hall, Clapham Junction, on 15 October, where Len Herbert's Sir Harry Barclay Cup award was announced.
items.s: ANNUAL DINNER AND DANCE Report of the club's Annual Dinner and Dance at the Express Hall, Clapham Junction, on 15 October, where Len Herbert's Sir Harry Barclay Cup award was announced. The Annual Dinner and Dance which was held at the Express Hall, Clapham Junction, on Saturday, October 15th. was again a huge success and the hall was filled to capacity. Despite the extensive enquiries of the Social Hon. Secretary, it was not possible to find a suitable hall which would hold a larger number of club members and it was with much regret that we were obliged to turn down applications for tickets. Bill Webb once again presided over the gathering and received a great ovation. The theme of Bill's few words in proposing “ The Club,” was the “ Belgrave Spirit,” and in replying to the toast, Secretary Alf Harley gave us some interesting data on the very early days of the club when handicap meetings were held on mid-week nights on the Embankment, lasting as late as eleven o'clock. During the course of the evening it was announced that Len Herbert had been awarded the Sir Harry Barclay Cup by the Surrey County A.A. for the best performance of 1949. The dance which followed dinner was very ably conducted by Bert Ellsey and our thanks are due to “ Dave ” for a very splendid evening. items.sum: Short items of news about Belgrave members at home and abroad, including appointments of R.W.A. judges and sympathy for Highgate walker R. Dick.
items.s: NEWS FROM MEMBERS Short items of news about Belgrave members at home and abroad, including appointments of R.W.A. judges and sympathy for Highgate walker R. Dick. Tony Whincup writes to say that having got over his exam. he is getting down to training. Tony Davis is soldiering at Horsham but says there's not much doing in the way of athletics. Jimmy Coates, one of our young walkers, who has recently emigrated to Canada, writes to say he is very impressed by the Canadian juniors but says there's a shortage of cinder tracks. Frank Thompson was a very welcome visitor at the A.G.M. He tells us that our old friend, Fred Rickards, who married again last year, has started another family and has a daughter. Good luck Fred, when are we going to see you again. Tommy Green is reported to be “ retiring ” from business and getting down to walking again. What about next year's National, Tommy? B. Lulham has passed his Coach's exam. for sprints and relays, and is now a A.A.A. Hon. Coach. Colin Sutton, settling down in Australia, is already winning races and is the district champion for 4½ miles. Stan Manning, who was ill last year, is now recovering and hopes to get to Wimbledon during the winter. Jack Rutland informs us that he will soon be out training again with an eye to long distance. Jack already holds an important executive post and he is now studying for further promotion. We all wish him luck. Syd Roberts and Frank Elson have been appointed R.W.A. judges. We have just learnt with regret of the serious accident which befel R. Dick, the popular and leading Highgate Harrier walker. We wish to express the club's sympathy with Mr. R. Dick and wish him a speedy and successful recovery. Tony Whincup Tony Whincup getting down to training after his exam.
